septic-tank-pumping.metaDescription: Septic tank pumping in Rosamond, CA for in-town homes and acre-plus desert parcels in Kern County. Locally owned crew from Lancaster. Call to schedule.
septic-tank-pumping.heroSub: Bought a Rosamond home with no pumping records, or just overdue on a rural parcel? We pump the tank, check the baffles and explain how it looked.
paragraphs: Rosamond homes trade hands often, partly because so many households are tied to jobs at Edwards Air Force Base, and pumping records rarely travel with the deed. A new owner may move into a house near Rosamond Boulevard or onto an acre of open desert with no idea whether the tank was serviced last year or a decade ago. That uncertainty is one of the most common reasons people call us for pumping here. Rentals add another layer, since tenants seldom know what a septic system can handle and landlords may not hear about slow drains until a backup forces the issue.

Pumping removes the sludge that settles on the tank floor and the scum that floats on top, before either layer can drift out toward the disposal area. In Rosamond that matters more than people expect. Caliche under the sandy topsoil already limits how fast a leach field or seepage pit can take water, and solids carried out of an overfull tank seal that soil even faster. A household that runs a garbage disposal or has extra people living in it may need visits closer together than the common three to five year guideline. We look at the liquid level and baffles while the lid is open.

Our crew comes north on SR-14 from Lancaster and treats in-town lots and outlying parcels the same way: find the lid, dig it out if blowing sand has covered it, pump the tank fully and break up the packed layer at the bottom. On larger rural lots we ask for directions past the last paved road and a note about where the truck can park, since hose runs can be long. Before we leave, you get a plain account of what we saw in the tank and whether anything deserves a closer look. Lancaster Septic Service is a locally owned outfit, so call us for a pumping visit or an on-site estimate.

faqs.q: I just bought a house in Rosamond and the seller had no pumping records. Should I pump right away?
faqs.a: It is usually a smart first step. Without records, there is no way to know how much sludge has built up, and pumping gives you a fresh starting point for your own schedule. While the tank is open we can tell you about the baffles and lids, which helps if the purchase inspection left questions. Kern County Environmental Health may hold older permit records for your parcel, so it can be worth asking them too.

faqs.q: Does Kern County require Rosamond septic tanks to be pumped on a set schedule?
faqs.a: Routine pumping for a single home is usually left to the owner rather than tied to a county calendar, but situations such as a sale, a repair or an addition may bring inspection or approval requirements. Rules can change, so Kern County Environmental Health is the office to ask about your specific property. We can explain what we find in the tank and what the county may want to see.

seepage-pit-pumping.metaDescription: Seepage pit pumping in Rosamond, CA for homes where caliche and desert storms slow drainage. Locally owned Antelope Valley crew. Call for a visit.
seepage-pit-pumping.heroSub: When a Rosamond seepage pit fills and stays full, we pump it, watch how quickly it recovers and tell you what the surrounding soil is doing.
paragraphs: Seepage pits do their work far below the surface, which is both their strength and their weakness in Rosamond. The sandy top layer drains well, but pockets of caliche deeper down can choke off the sidewalls of a pit, leaving effluent with fewer places to go. On the flat lots around town, a rare heavy storm can also send runoff sheeting across the yard and pooling right over the pit cover, loading the surrounding ground at the worst possible moment. Owners usually notice the result as slow tubs and toilets that recover for a while and then slow down again.

Pumping a pit is different from pumping a tank. We draw down the liquid, remove the sludge and fine material that has settled at the bottom, and then watch how quickly water seeps back in from the soil. That recovery rate tells us a lot. A pit that refills slowly after pumping may only need its tank serviced more often, while one that floods back fast may be sitting in saturated or sealed ground. On older Rosamond homes the tank and pit were often installed together, so we usually check the tank at the same visit and compare the two.

Pit covers in Rosamond often turn up under drifted sand or gravel, so let us know if you have ever seen the access point or have a sketch from a previous owner. Rural parcels toward Willow Springs or along the dirt roads east of town may need longer hose runs, and a note about gate access helps us plan the trip. After pumping, we explain whether the pit looks like it has useful life left or whether it is time to talk about a replacement pit or added disposal area. Call to set up a visit and an honest look at how your pit is draining.

faqs.q: Why does my Rosamond seepage pit fill up again after a winter storm?
faqs.a: Flat desert lots do not shed water well, so heavy rain can soak the ground around a pit and leave it with little room to absorb household water. Caliche below the sand can slow that drying even more. Pumping can buy time while the soil dries out, but if the pit refills quickly in dry weather too, the sidewalls may be sealed and a longer-term fix may be needed.

faqs.q: Will I need approval from Kern County to add a new seepage pit next to my old one?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Adding or replacing a disposal pit is the kind of work Kern County Environmental Health may want to look over before it starts, and they may ask about soil testing and setbacks on your lot. Requirements vary by parcel, so contact them early. We can walk your property, describe what we see in the existing pit and talk through what the county may ask for.

septic-inspection.metaDescription: Septic inspections in Rosamond, CA for escrow, rentals and rural Kern County homes. Plain written findings from a locally owned crew. Call to book.
septic-inspection.heroSub: Buying, selling or renting out a Rosamond home? We open the tank, check the parts that matter and give you findings you can share with a lender.
paragraphs: A lot of Rosamond homes go up for sale on short notice, since many owners work at Edwards Air Force Base and move when their jobs do. That pace leaves little room for surprises, and the septic system is one of the few parts of a house a buyer cannot judge by walking through it. Lenders and buyers often ask for a septic inspection during escrow, and sellers sometimes order one first so the results do not become a last-minute problem. Landlords with rentals in town also use inspections to check on a system between tenants.

An inspection here starts with the tank. We open it, measure the sludge and scum layers, look at the baffles, walls and lid, and run water from the house to watch how the system handles flow. Then we check the disposal side, whether that is a leach field on an acre parcel or a seepage pit behind an older home near Rosamond Boulevard. Desert conditions leave their own marks: sand inside poorly sealed risers, concrete lids cracked by years of hot days and cold nights, and slow drainage where caliche sits under the field.

You get a written summary in plain terms, with notes on anything that needs attention now and anything worth watching. If the tank is due for pumping, we can usually do both at one visit so we can see the walls and floor of the empty tank. Since Rosamond is in Kern County, any inspection rules tied to a sale or repair come from Kern County Environmental Health rather than Los Angeles County, and we can explain what may apply to your situation. Call to set up an inspection or to ask what the visit will cover for your property.

faqs.q: Is a septic inspection required to sell a house in Rosamond?
faqs.a: It depends on the sale. Kern County may not require one for every transfer, but many lenders and buyers ask for an inspection during escrow, and some loan programs may want one. Check with your agent, your lender and Kern County Environmental Health about your situation. Having an inspection done early gives a seller time to handle any repairs before they become a negotiating point.

faqs.q: My rental in Rosamond has had several tenants. What should an inspection look for?
faqs.a: Tenant turnover often means nobody tracked what went down the drains. We look for heavy sludge, wipes or grease in the tank, damaged baffles and signs that solids have moved toward the field or pit. We also check that lids are secure and easy to reach, since blowing sand tends to bury them. The findings help you set a pumping schedule and decide whether anything needs repair before the next lease.

septic-repair.metaDescription: Septic system repair in Rosamond, CA for broken baffles, cracked lids, damaged lines and alarms. Locally owned crew serving Kern County. Call us.
septic-repair.heroSub: From a cracked lid on a windswept lot to a broken baffle in town, we find what failed in your Rosamond system and fix that part.
paragraphs: Most septic repairs we see in Rosamond start small. A plastic riser lid goes brittle after years of summer sun and cold nights, a seal loosens, and wind-driven sand starts sifting into the tank. An old concrete lid develops a crack that lets dust and rain in. Inside the tank, a baffle that has corroded away lets scum drift toward the outlet. None of these problems announce themselves at first, but each one shortens the life of the leach field or seepage pit downstream, and that part of the system is far harder to replace on caliche ground.

The first job on any repair is finding the real cause, because a backup in a Rosamond home can come from several places. A clogged inlet, a sagging line between the house and tank, a full tank or a pit that has stopped draining all look similar from inside the bathroom. We open the tank, check the levels and baffles and, where needed, run a camera through the line before recommending anything. You hear the fix and the reason for it before we start, and we repair the part that failed rather than pushing for a full replacement.

Repairs on Rosamond rentals and on small businesses along Rosamond Boulevard often have to fit around tenants, customers and parking, so tell us when the work causes the least disruption. Larger repairs, especially anything that changes the tank or disposal area, may need a look from Kern County Environmental Health, and we can talk through what the county may want before work begins. For outlying parcels, let us know about gates and soft sand on the access road. Call to describe the problem, and we will set up a visit to look at it on site.

faqs.q: Sand keeps getting into my septic tank in Rosamond. Can that be fixed?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Sand tends to enter through a cracked lid, a loose riser joint or a riser cover that no longer seals. Replacing the lid, resealing the riser or adding a gasketed cover often stops it. Sand that has already settled in the tank takes up space meant for wastewater, so pumping it out at the same visit helps. We can look at the opening and tell you which fix makes sense.

faqs.q: Do I need a Kern County permit to repair my septic system in Rosamond?
faqs.a: It depends on the repair. Small fixes like replacing a baffle or a lid may not need approval, while larger work such as replacing a tank, adding to a leach field or installing a new pit may require sign-off from Kern County Environmental Health. Rules vary, so call them about your specific project. We can describe the repair we recommend so you know exactly what to ask.

leach-field-repair.metaDescription: Leach field repair in Rosamond, CA for soggy ground, slow drains and fields sitting on caliche. Locally owned Antelope Valley crew. Call to schedule.
leach-field-repair.heroSub: On Rosamond's flat desert lots, a struggling leach field often shows up as slow drains or damp ground. We find out why and recommend a fix that fits.
paragraphs: The open parcels around Rosamond give most homes plenty of room for a leach field, yet room is not the same as good drainage. Under the loose sand there are often caliche layers that water moves through slowly, and a field laid out above one of those layers can struggle from the day it goes in. Add years of solids escaping from a tank that was not pumped often enough, and a crust called biomat forms along the trenches. The field still takes some water, just not enough, so drains slow down after laundry or showers stack up.

Flat ground plays a role too. When a rare heavy storm moves through, water can sheet across a Rosamond lot and pool over the trenches, flooding a field that was already near its limit. Signs to watch for include damp or unusually green strips in an otherwise dry yard, sewage odor near the disposal area, and gurgling in the lowest drains. Before recommending anything, we check the tank, the distribution box and the lines to rule out simpler causes, since a crushed pipe or a blocked outlet can make a healthy field look like it has failed.

Repair options depend on what we find. Some fields recover after the tank is pumped, the lines are jetted and water use is spread out. Others need new trenches placed in better soil elsewhere on the parcel, which is possible on many acre lots in town and toward Willow Springs. Work that adds or relocates trenches may need approval from Kern County Environmental Health, and soil testing could be part of that. We walk the field with you, lay out the options in plain terms and give an on-site estimate. Lancaster Septic Service is locally owned, so call to set up that visit.

faqs.q: My Rosamond lot is an acre. Can a new leach field go somewhere else on the property?
faqs.a: Often it can. Larger parcels usually have room for new trenches, but placement depends on setbacks from property lines, buildings and any well, plus how the soil drains in that spot. Caliche can make one corner of a lot drain far better than another. Kern County Environmental Health may ask for soil testing before approving a new location, and we can explain what that process may involve.

faqs.q: Should I stop using water after a storm floods my leach field?
faqs.a: Cutting back helps. Spread out laundry, take shorter showers and hold off on the dishwasher until the ground over the trenches dries. A Rosamond field under standing water has nowhere to send effluent, so heavy use can push sewage back toward the house. If drains stay slow once the yard has dried, the field may have a deeper problem, and we can come check the tank, lines and trenches.

septic-installation.metaDescription: Septic installation and replacement in Rosamond, CA for rural parcels and older homes in Kern County. Plain planning help from a locally owned crew.
septic-installation.heroSub: Replacing a worn-out system in an older Rosamond home or planning one for an open desert parcel, we help you work through layout, soil and next steps.
paragraphs: Many of the older homes around Rosamond still run on the system that came with the house, and some of those tanks and pits are near the end of their working life. Replacement usually becomes the topic when repairs stop holding, when the disposal area keeps flooding, or when an inspection during a sale turns up a failed tank. On larger desert parcels the question is often not whether there is room for a new system but where the soil will actually take water, since caliche can sit under one part of a lot and not another.

Planning comes first. Kern County Environmental Health usually needs to look at plans for new and replacement systems, and they may ask for soil or percolation testing, a site plan and setbacks from the house, property lines and any well. Results from that testing help decide between a leach field and a seepage pit and how large either needs to be. A homeowner should also think about where the truck will reach the new tank for future pumping, and whether risers will bring the lids to grade so blowing sand does not hide them.

From layout through backfill, we help Rosamond owners think through placement, set the new tank and build the disposal area, then walk you through how the system works and what it needs. We explain each step before it happens and talk through what Kern County may ask for along the way, though the approval itself comes from the county. Rural lots off dirt roads need room for equipment, so let us know about access early. Call to set up an on-site look, and we will talk through what your parcel can support.

faqs.q: Does caliche on my Rosamond lot rule out a new septic system?
faqs.a: Not usually, but it can change the design. Caliche slows water, so testing may show that one part of the lot drains better than another, or that a deeper seepage pit or a larger field is needed to get below or around the hard layer. Kern County Environmental Health may require testing results before approving a layout. We can look at the site and talk through options.

faqs.q: What happens to the old tank when a Rosamond home gets a new system?
faqs.a: The old tank is usually pumped out and then either removed or filled in place so it cannot collapse later. Kern County may have requirements for how an abandoned tank is handled, so it is worth confirming with Kern County Environmental Health before work begins. We will explain what we plan to do with the old tank as part of the replacement estimate, so there are no loose ends.

septic-risers.metaDescription: Septic riser and lid installation in Rosamond, CA. Bring buried tank lids to grade so blowing sand stops hiding them. Locally owned crew. Call us.
septic-risers.heroSub: Rosamond wind can bury a tank lid between one pumping and the next. A sealed riser brings access to grade so nobody has to dig every visit.
paragraphs: Ask a Rosamond homeowner how long it took to find their tank lid last time, and the answer often involves a shovel and a lot of guessing. Wind moves sand across yards here constantly, and a lid that was easy to spot after one pumping can sit under several inches of drift by the next. Older homes in town and rural parcels out toward Edwards Air Force Base alike tend to have lids buried well below grade. Every visit then starts with digging, which adds time, disturbs the yard and leaves a soft patch of ground behind.

A riser is a short shaft, usually plastic or concrete, that extends from the tank opening up to the surface and is capped with a secure lid. In Rosamond, the seal matters as much as the height. A riser with gaps at the joints lets dust and sand sift into the tank, and a cheap lid can warp or crack after a few seasons of summer heat and cold nights. We seal each joint and use lids made for long outdoor sun exposure. Locking or screw-down lids also keep children and pets out of the tank.

Risers usually go in at the same visit as a pumping, since the lids are already exposed. We dig to the tank, fit the riser to the opening, seal it, backfill and set the lid flush or slightly above grade so it can be found under light drifting. On open parcels, a lid sitting just above the ground is easy to spot from the driveway. Tell us whether you prefer plastic or concrete and whether vehicles ever cross that part of the yard. Call to schedule riser installation in Rosamond or ask for an on-site estimate.

faqs.q: Will a septic riser in Rosamond get buried by sand too?
faqs.a: Less often. Setting the lid at or slightly above grade means a light drift may cover it, but a quick sweep usually finds it instead of a dig. Some owners add a small marker beside the lid so it stays visible on windy lots. A riser with a sealed lid also keeps that sand out of the tank itself, which is the bigger benefit over time.

faqs.q: Do I need permission from Kern County to add a riser to my tank?
faqs.a: Adding a riser usually does not change how the system works, but Kern County Environmental Health may have rules about lids, access and how risers are secured. Requirements can differ by situation, so a quick check with them is worthwhile before the work. We can describe exactly what we plan to install, including lid type and height, so you know what to ask.

grease-trap-pumping.metaDescription: Grease trap pumping in Rosamond, CA for restaurants, cafes and food businesses along Rosamond Boulevard. Locally owned crew. Call to schedule.
grease-trap-pumping.heroSub: For kitchens along Rosamond Boulevard and elsewhere in town, we pump grease traps and interceptors and keep a service record for your files.
paragraphs: Most of Rosamond's food businesses sit along Rosamond Boulevard, mixed in with the other shops that serve the town. Whether a kitchen drains to a sewer connection or to a septic system on its own lot, a grease trap or interceptor is what keeps fats, oils and food scraps from leaving the building. When that trap fills, the grease moves on, and on a septic property it can coat the tank and seal the disposal area, which is hard to fix on caliche ground. Along the way, it leaves slow sinks, odors and clogged floor drains behind.

Pumping a grease trap means removing the floating grease layer, the water below it and the solids that settle to the bottom, then scraping the walls and checking the baffles or tees that keep grease inside. How often that needs to happen depends on menu, volume and trap size, so a small cafe with a short menu may need service less often than a busy restaurant with a full grill line. Health or sewer agencies may set a schedule for your business, and Kern County Environmental Health can tell you what applies.

We work around service hours, which matters for small Rosamond restaurants where closing the kitchen even briefly costs sales. Tell us when you open, when deliveries arrive and whether the trap is inside under a sink or out in the parking area, since tight parking near the Boulevard shops can affect where the truck sets up. After each pumping we note the date, the condition of the trap and anything that looked off, so you have a record ready if an inspector asks. Call to set up a first service or a regular schedule.

faqs.q: My Rosamond cafe is on a septic system. Does that change how often the grease trap needs pumping?
faqs.a: It can. On a septic property, any grease that slips past the trap ends up in the tank and can seal the soil in the leach field or pit, which is costly to fix. Many owners pump the trap a little more often to protect the system behind it. We can look at your trap size and kitchen volume and suggest a schedule, and Kern County may have its own requirements.

faqs.q: Can you pump our grease trap before lunch so we do not lose customers on Rosamond Boulevard?
faqs.a: In most cases we can plan the visit around your hours. Early morning before opening or the slow stretch in the afternoon usually works best for small kitchens. Let us know where the trap sits and where the truck can park, since space along the Boulevard can be tight at midday. We will confirm a time with you before the visit so your staff can plan around it.

emergency-septic-service.metaDescription: Emergency septic service in Rosamond, CA for backups, overflowing tanks and alarms. Call us and we will get a truck north as soon as we can.
emergency-septic-service.heroSub: Sewage in the tub or a tank overflowing in your Rosamond yard? Call and describe it, and we will get a truck out as soon as we can.
paragraphs: Septic emergencies in Rosamond tend to follow a pattern. A household on a rural parcel lives with slow drains for a few weeks, a full house or a heavy laundry day pushes the system past its limit, and sewage comes up in the lowest shower or toilet. Storms cause their own trouble here, since water sheeting across flat lots can flood a leach field or seepage pit and leave household water with nowhere to go. A lid buried by drifting sand can make the situation slower to fix, because the tank has to be found before anything else happens.

While you wait for the truck, stop running water anywhere in the house. Hold off on laundry, dishwashers and flushing, and keep children and pets away from any wet area in the yard. If sewage has come into the house, avoid touching it without gloves and keep the room ventilated. It also helps to think about where the tank and any cleanouts are, and whether a gate or soft sand on the access road could slow the truck down. Those details matter most on the dirt roads north and east of Rosamond Boulevard.

Coming up SR-14 from Lancaster, we need a few details when you call: the street or nearest cross road, a description of the problem and anything you know about the system. We will get a truck out as soon as we can. On site, we usually pump the tank first to relieve the backup, then look for the cause, whether that is a blocked inlet, a broken baffle, a crushed line or a disposal area that has stopped draining. You hear what we found and what a lasting fix would involve before any repair work begins.

faqs.q: Who do I call first if sewage backs up into my Rosamond home, a plumber or a septic company?
faqs.a: If the backup shows up in several drains, especially the lowest ones, the septic system is a likely cause, and a septic crew can check the tank level right away. If only one sink or toilet is affected, a plumbing clog inside the house may be the issue. Call us and describe what you see, and we will help you sort out which it likely is.

faqs.q: My lot near Willow Springs has a gate and a sandy road. Can a pump truck still get in?
faqs.a: Usually, yes, but tell us about it when you call. Deep sand or a narrow gate can change where the truck parks, and long hose runs let us reach tanks that sit far from the driveway. Leaving the gate open or meeting us at the road saves time in an emergency. If the road is washed out after a storm, let us know so we can plan another approach.

septic-line-jetting.metaDescription: Septic line jetting and camera inspection in Rosamond, CA. Clear grease, sand and roots from sewer lines and see the pipe on video. Call our crew.
septic-line-jetting.heroSub: Drains in your Rosamond home that clog again and again usually point to a line problem. We jet the pipe clean and show you the camera footage.
paragraphs: On many Rosamond parcels the line from the house to the tank, and from the tank to the field or pit, runs a long way across open ground. Long runs in sandy soil give a pipe more chances to settle and sag, and a low spot in the line collects grease and paper until drains slow down. Rentals add wipes and cooking grease that tenants did not know to keep out. When a clog keeps coming back after the tank has been pumped, the pipe itself is usually the next place to look, and guessing from the surface rarely finds it.

Jetting sends water through the line at high pressure from a nozzle that scours the full width of the pipe, washing grease, sludge and loose sand toward the tank where it can be pumped out. The camera follows on a cable and shows what water alone cannot tell us: a cracked joint, a belly where the ground settled, or a section crushed under a driveway. Lines into a leach field can slowly fill with sludge, and on caliche ground that buildup slows drainage even further, so we often look at the laterals too when the field is struggling.

Most visits begin with a camera pass to make sure the line can take the pressure, then we jet and check again to confirm it is clear. You watch the footage with us, and if there is damage, we mark the spot on the ground so a repair only opens the yard where it needs to. If your cleanout is buried under drifted sand or gravel, tell us before the visit so we can plan to find it. Lancaster Septic Service is locally owned and close by, so call to schedule line jetting and a camera inspection in Rosamond.

faqs.q: Can sand get into septic lines in Rosamond?
faqs.a: It can. Sand usually enters through a cracked pipe, an open cleanout cap or a joint that has separated as the ground shifted. Once inside, it settles in low spots and traps grease and paper. Jetting flushes the sand toward the tank, and the camera shows where it got in, so the actual entry point can be repaired rather than cleared over and over.

faqs.q: Should I pump my Rosamond tank at the same visit as line jetting?
faqs.a: It usually makes sense. Jetting pushes grease, sludge and debris from the line into the tank, so pumping afterward removes it instead of leaving it to settle. If the tank is close to due anyway, combining the two saves a second trip out to your property. We can check your tank level when we arrive and recommend whether pumping is worth doing that day.

septic-tank-locating.metaDescription: Septic tank locating in Rosamond, CA. We find buried tanks and lids on in-town lots and open desert parcels, mark them and note depth. Call us.
septic-tank-locating.heroSub: Lost track of the tank on your Rosamond property? We trace the line, uncover the lids under the sand and mark them for next time.
paragraphs: Because Rosamond sits just past Avenue A and the county line, people who move up from Lancaster or Palmdale sometimes go looking for septic records in the wrong place. Any permit drawings for a Rosamond home would generally be with Kern County, not Los Angeles County, and older files may be thin or missing. Out on an acre parcel with no fences or landscaping to measure from, a tank can be hard to pin down even with a sketch. Wind adds to the problem by smoothing over the ground and hiding any marker an earlier owner left behind.

Locating starts where the sewer line leaves the house. A small transmitter goes into the pipe through a cleanout, and a receiver above ground picks up its signal, showing direction and depth as we walk the yard until the signal stops at the tank. A steel probe confirms the spot, then we dig to the lids and measure them from fixed points like house corners. On sandy Rosamond lots the probe usually slides in easily, though caliche can make it harder to tell a buried lid from a hard layer, so we confirm before calling it found.

Knowing the location pays off right away. Pumping and inspections go faster, escrow is simpler, and you avoid parking trucks or trailers over the tank on an open lot where that can be tempting. Many Rosamond owners have us add a riser once the lids are exposed, so the search never has to be repeated. Before we come out, gather any paperwork from the purchase and tell us about buried sprinkler lines or recent grading. Call to schedule tank locating, and you will get a simple sketch to keep with your home records.

faqs.q: Where would septic records for my Rosamond home be kept?
faqs.a: Since Rosamond is in Kern County, any permit records or drawings would generally be with Kern County Environmental Health rather than Los Angeles County. Older homes may have little on file, and what exists may not show the current layout if the house or yard has changed. A previous owner's pumping receipts sometimes note the tank location too. If records come up empty, we can find the tank on site.

faqs.q: Can you find a tank on a big open lot with nothing to measure from?
faqs.a: Yes. We trace the line from the house to the tank electronically, so the search follows the pipe rather than relying on landmarks. Once we find the lids, we measure from the house corners or another fixed point and note the depth. On large Rosamond parcels, a riser or a small marker post afterward makes the tank easy to spot from a distance, even after a windy season.
